description: The City of Palaces – a royal blend of heritage, culture, and vibrant markets. Famous for its grand Dasara celebrations and beautiful Mysore Palace.
popular_places: Mysore Palace, Chamundi Hills, Brindavan Gardens, Zoo, Devaraja Market
student_tip: Visit Mysore Palace during evening illumination (Tue/Sat/Sun) for a magical experience. It's free with student ID on certain days.

description: India's Silicon Valley – a cosmopolitan city with vibrant cafes, parks, tech culture, and nightlife. Perfect for student exploration.
popular_places: Lalbagh Garden, Cubbon Park, Vidhana Soudha, Commercial Street, Nandi Hills, ISKCON Temple
student_tip: Use the Namma Metro for super cheap city travel. Student discounts available at many museums.

description: Misty coffee hills, lush forests, and serene trekking trails. A paradise for nature lovers and adventure seekers.
popular_places: Mullayanagiri Peak, Baba Budangiri, Hebbe Falls, Coffee Estates, Kudremukh
student_tip: Book homestays in coffee estates – usually very affordable and include fresh coffee and breakfast.

description: The Scotland of India – emerald coffee and spice plantations, waterfalls, and cool misty air. Ideal for a refreshing student trip.
popular_places: Abbey Falls, Raja's Seat, Dubare Elephant Camp, Talakaveri, Namdroling Monastery
student_tip: Travel in groups to split costs on rented bikes. Local coffee shops serve amazing filter coffee at ₹20.

description: A UNESCO World Heritage site – a surreal landscape of ancient ruins, boulders, and temples along the Tungabhadra River.
popular_places: Virupaksha Temple, Vittala Temple, Matanga Hill, Hemakuta Hill, Elephant Stables
student_tip: Rent a bicycle (₹100-150/day) to explore all ruins at your own pace. Very student friendly.

description: Coastal Karnataka's gem – famous for its Udupi cuisine, Krishna Temple, pristine beaches, and relaxed vibe.
popular_places: Udupi Krishna Temple, Malpe Beach, St. Mary's Island, Manipal, Kaup Beach
student_tip: The Udupi darshini restaurants offer amazing authentic food for ₹30-80 per meal. Try the masala dosa!

description: A bustling port city blending beaches, heritage churches, tasty coastal cuisine, and easy access to Goa and Kerala.
popular_places: Panambur Beach, Kadri Manjunath Temple, Kudroli Temple, Sultan Battery, Tannirbhavi Beach
student_tip: Local KSRTC buses are very cheap. Try fish thali at local restaurants for ₹80-120.

description: India's beach paradise – sun, sand, shacks, water sports, flea markets, and a laid-back vibe loved by students.
popular_places: Baga Beach, Anjuna Flea Market, Fort Aguada, Dudhsagar Falls, Old Goa Churches
student_tip: Travel during the off-season (May-June) for much cheaper accommodation. Use local buses (₹10-20) instead of taxis.

description: The Queen of Hill Stations – rolling tea gardens, a scenic toy train, and cool mountain air make it perfect for a student retreat.
best_time: April to June / October to December
popular_places: Ooty Lake, Doddabetta Peak, Botanical Gardens, Tea Factory, Nilgiri Mountain Railway
student_tip: The toy train experience costs only ₹20-50 (unreserved) and is absolutely stunning. Book early!

description: The City of Nizams – biryani, Charminar, Golconda Fort, tech parks, and a rich blend of old-world charm and modern energy.
popular_places: Charminar, Golconda Fort, Ramoji Film City, Hussain Sagar, Salar Jung Museum
student_tip: Affordable city buses and metro. Try biryani at Shadab or Paradise for ₹150-200 – authentic and filling.
